shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from balanced (1,1,1) to less varied (1,0,2), and I value variety, so this reduces my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, trading 1×B for 1×A would make my inventory less balanced (C:1, A:2, B:0). Since I value variety, this lowers my utility.
Trading 1×B for 2×A increases my total goods, and after the trade I still keep some variety while improving my bundle overall.
I currently have equal amounts of C, A, and B. Trading 1 C for 1 B would reduce variety by leaving me with no C and extra B, which lowers my utility.
I currently have equal amounts of all goods, so swapping 1×B for 1×C would reduce variety and make my bundle less balanced.
Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C increases my total goods, and after the trade I still keep variety across all three goods.
I value A and B equally, and with an even inventory this trade would only swap one good for another, reducing variety rather than improving my bundle.
I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C. Trading 1×B for 1×A would make my bundle less balanced (A:2, B:0, C:1), which reduces variety and does not improve my utility.
Starting from an even bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (1,3,0). The gain in total goods outweighs the loss of variety, so this increases my utility.
Starting from an even mix of 1 C, 1 A, and 1 B, exchanging 1 C for 1 B would make my bundle less balanced (0 C, 1 A, 2 B). Since I value variety, this lowers my utility.
Trading 1 B for 1 C changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (2,1,0), reducing variety. Since I value goods equally and prefer balanced holdings, this does not increase my utility.
Starting from an even 1/1/1 bundle, giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory to C=3, A=1, B=0. This increases my total goods and is favorable despite reducing variety.

Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by adding a good I currently lack entirely, changing my bundle from (C2,A2,B0) to (C2,A1,B1). Since I value goods equally and prefer having more of what I have less of, this increases my utility.

I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B strongly improves my variety. Giving 2 A reduces a surplus good and leaves me with a balanced bundle of 2 C, 0 A, 1 B; despite B being scarce, this trade still increases my utility from having more variety.
This trade increases variety by converting one surplus C into one scarce B, improving my balanced bundle from (2C,2A,0B) to (1C,2A,1B).

This trade increases variety in my inventory by gaining my scarcest good, B, while reducing a good I currently have more of, C. Moving from (C2, A2, B0) to (C0, A2, B1) improves my balance, and B is also currently harder to obtain.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety: I currently have no B, and B is especially valuable both because I lack it and because market scarcity makes obtaining B harder.
This trade increases my variety by acquiring my scarcest good, B, which I currently have none of. Giving 2 A reduces a surplus good and leaves me with a more balanced bundle.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves my variety by converting a surplus good into one I currently lack, and B is also relatively scarce in the market.
I currently have no B, so gaining 1 B significantly improves variety. Giving 2 C leaves me with a more balanced bundle (A:2, B:1, C:0), and B is also harder to obtain in the market.

I currently have one of each good, which is perfectly balanced for my variety preference. Trading 1×A for 1×B would make my bundle less balanced (C:1, A:0, B:2), so it reduces my utility despite B being scarcer in the market.
The trade changes my inventory from (1C,1A,1B) to (1C,2A,0B), reducing variety by eliminating B. Since I value goods equally and prefer a balanced mix, this lowers my utility.
Giving up my only B reduces variety and sacrifices a good that is currently scarce in the market. Receiving 2 A would leave me overconcentrated in A rather than improving balance.
I currently have one of each good, which is maximally balanced for my variety preference. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make my bundle less balanced (0 C, 1 A, 2 B), so it does not increase my utility.

Starting from an even 1A/1B/1C bundle, trading away 1 B for 1 C would reduce variety and leave me with 0 B, which lowers my utility. The market also indicates B is relatively scarce, making this exchange especially unfavorable.

Giving up my only B would reduce variety, and B is currently scarcer in the market, increasing its relative value. Moving from {A:1,B:1,C:1} to {A:1,B:0,C:3} worsens my balanced bundle despite gaining more C.
Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by converting a surplus good into one I currently lack, and B is also relatively scarce in the market.

I currently lack B entirely, so gaining 1 B greatly improves my variety. Trading 2 A for 1 B changes my bundle from (C1,A2,B0) to (C1,A0,B1), which is more balanced and increases my utility; B is also currently scarce in the market.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety in my inventory by turning a duplicate type into a missing type. With B scarce and I currently have none, receiving 1 B increases my utility.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:2, A:0, B:2), which reduces variety by eliminating A and increasing a good I already have less need for. This does not improve my bundle under my preference for balanced variety.
A and B are equally valued in general, and I currently have the same amount of each. Trading 1×B for 1×A would not improve variety or increase my utility.

This improves variety and increases my lower-held good A while reducing B, which I do not have in greater quantity than A after the trade. Going from (C2, A1, B1) to (C2, A3, B0) gives me more total goods, and receiving 2 A for 1 B is favorable enough to increase my utility.

Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (C2, A1, B1) to (C1, A1, B2). Since I value variety and currently have more C than B, giving up a surplus C for a scarcer B is acceptable and keeps my bundle balanced overall.

Trading 1 B for 1 C changes my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:3, A:1, B:0). Since B and A are currently my scarcer goods, giving up my only B reduces variety and lowers my utility more than gaining an extra C helps.

This would change my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:0, A:1, B:2), making my bundle less balanced by overconcentrating in B and eliminating C. Since I value variety and currently C is not less valuable than B, giving 2 C for 1 B does not improve my utility.

Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (C2, A1, B1) to (C4, A1, B0). Since B is currently one of my scarcer goods, losing it hurts variety, but receiving two units for one makes the trade favorable overall.
Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from {C:1, A:1, B:0} to {C:1, A:0, B:1}, which increases variety by adding the good I currently lack.
Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from {C:1, A:1, B:0} to {C:0, A:1, B:1}, which improves variety by filling the good I currently lack.

Trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory from (C2,A1,B1) to (C2,A0,B2). Since A and B are currently tied as my least-held goods, this exchange is utility-neutral rather than harmful, so accepting is acceptable.

Trading 1 B for 1 A changes my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:2, A:2, B:0), which reduces variety. Since A and B are equally valued in general and I currently have less of B than A after the trade, giving up B for A lowers my utility.
Giving 1 B (which I have 1 of) and receiving 2 A increases my total goods from 4 to 5, and the gain outweighs the loss even though it reduces variety somewhat.
Trading 1 C for 1 B would change my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:1, A:1, B:2), which does not improve variety overall and simply swaps my current surplus from C to B.

Trading 1 B for 1 C changes my inventory from (C:2, A:1, B:1) to (C:3, A:1, B:0), which reduces variety by eliminating B. Since I value goods equally but prefer balancing lower-count goods, giving up my only B lowers my utility.
Giving 2×C would leave me with none of a currently more-needed good, while receiving 1×B increases an item I already have; this reduces variety and does not improve my bundle.

Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from C2/A1/B1 to C4/A1/B0. Since A and B are currently my scarcest goods, losing my only B reduces variety more than the extra C helps, so this does not improve my utility.
Trading 1 B for 1 A changes my inventory from {C:1, A:0, B:1} to {C:1, A:1, B:0}, giving me a more balanced bundle and increasing variety, which improves my utility.
Giving 1 B and receiving 2 A changes my inventory from {C:1, A:0, B:1} to {C:1, A:2, B:0}. Since I currently have no A, gaining A increases variety and improves my bundle despite giving up B.
Giving 1 C and receiving 1 B would change my inventory from C:1, A:0, B:1 to C:0, A:0, B:2, reducing variety and increasing a good I already have while losing one I have less of.

This trade increases variety by swapping an extra B for C, changing my inventory from C1/A0/B1 to C2/A0/B0. Since I currently lack A but cannot affect A in this offer, exchanging one equally valued good for another is acceptable and does not reduce utility.

Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (C:1, A:0, B:1) to (C:3, A:0, B:0). Since I currently have no A and only one each of B and C, B and C are similarly valued before the trade; receiving two units for one unit given increases my overall holdings and improves utility despite reducing variety.
